parties: Aegis Logistics Limited (India) in talks to acquire Tristar Group (UAE-based, subsidiary of Kuwait's Agility Global PLC)
headline: Aegis Logistics in talks to acquire UAE's Tristar for $1.5 billion - NSE seeks clarification
sum: NSE sought clarification from Aegis Logistics on a rumoured $1.5 billion acquisition of Tristar, a UAE-based fuel logistics subsidiary of Kuwait's Agility Global. No formal announcement or confirmation has been publicly disclosed as of 18 August 2026.
implication: Cross-border energy logistics consolidation-if confirmed, would mark Aegis's first major international platform acquisition, expanding beyond India's coast-based terminal network into Middle East fuel storage and distribution.
detail: The NSE requested news verification from Aegis Logistics regarding reports it was in talks to acquire Tristar Group for $1.5 billion. Tristar is a Dubai-headquartered, fully-integrated energy logistics provider owned by Kuwait's Agility Global. No response, confirmation or denial has been disclosed publicly. The transaction remains unconfirmed and the only source is the NSE clarification request itself. Agility had previously announced in September 2024 it was considering stake sales in Tristar to unlock value for shareholders.

framework.note: RBI approval required for outbound investment by Indian entity; FEMA Regulation 2015 governs cross-border M&A

framework.ref: Acquisition of Control Norms under Regulation 30, SEBI (LODR) Regulations 2015
framework.note: Material event disclosure and fair pricing norms apply if acquisition is material to acquiring company
CCI merger control clearance required if transaction meets threshold (assets/turnover >Rs. 2,000 cr)
Vessel registration and coastal shipping rules may apply if maritime assets cross borders
Regulatory clearance for fuel storage, distribution and terminalling assets in UAE/Middle East
Board and shareholder approval for acquisition of subsidiary/ asset sale by Aegis

framework.ref: UAE Commercial Companies Law & Dubai Free Zone Authority (DFZA) regulations
framework.note: Approval from target company's local jurisdiction for change of control and foreign investment

conditions: CCI merger control clearance (if turnover/asset threshold breached)
UAE regulatory clearances for change of control and foreign investment
approvals: NSE/BSE (SEBI LODR Regulation 30 disclosure and approval)
structure.novel: If confirmed, would represent Aegis's first material outbound acquisition into Middle East fuel logistics, a departure from India-focused terminal operations. Cross-border USD-denominated transaction at >₹12,000+ crore valuation.

triggers.law: Foreign Exchange Management Act 1999 / FEMA Regulations 2015
triggers.note: Outbound direct investment by Indian company requires RBI approval; valuation and strategic rationale subject to review
If combined turnover of parties exceeds ₹2,000 cr or assets exceed ₹1,000 cr, CCI filing and approval required
Acquisition of a target with >10% of acquirer's net worth or >5% of consolidated turnover is 'material' and requires disclosure within 30 minutes of price-sensitive information being made public
